how: the note's mathematics, checked on main (checks/web_weave_action_on_tau.py). Its section 3 is proved there in two lines and the proof holds: an invariant C^1 function has a differential fixed by a rotation of order 2 at i and of order 3 at omega, and a linear form fixed by a non-trivial rotation is zero. Numerically, for log(y |eta|^4), E(tau, 3) and E(tau, 2): the gradient is below 2e-9 at i and omega and of order 0.2 to 6 at a generic point; y |eta|^4 has a saddle at i (Hessian -1.298, 0.298) and its maximum at omega (-0.667 twice); E(tau, 3) and E(tau, 2) have a saddle at i and their minimum at omega and grow to the cusp (4.659, 4.141, 16.89, 130.4 at i, omega, 2i, 4i). The mirror-line consequence and the torsion-free remark for lines of order 4 or more are by hand from the same argument (B1809's lemma is main's)
